subject: Learning Methods
title: Temperature and Sleep Quality
description: A quick, practical guide to Temperature and Sleep Quality.

hook.text: Your body needs to drop its core temperature by about one degree Celsius to fall asleep. A hot room fights this process.

buildup.text: The ideal bedroom temperature for sleep is 18–19 degrees Celsius. Most people keep their rooms too warm for optimal.

discovery.text: A warm bath before bed paradoxically helps. It draws blood to the skin surface, which then radiates heat, cooling.

twist.text: Cold hands and feet prevent sleep initiation because the body can't radiate heat.

climax.text: Cool room, warm extremities. Set your thermostat to 18 degrees, take a warm shower before bed, and keep your feet.

punchline.text: Cool the room. Warm the feet. Sleep comes faster.

quiz.question: Why does a warm bath before bed help with sleep?
options: Warm water relaxes muscles that were tense from the day
It draws blood to the surface, radiating heat and cooling the core
The steam clears nasal passages for better breathing
